opportunities.title: When does automation become an AI enabled enrollment scheme?
opportunities.question: Which technical evidence distinguishes human impersonation, scripts, and generative AI in confirmed enrollment fraud?
opportunities.design: Compare adjudicated identity fraud cases with institutional reports that explicitly identify automation. Code AI attribution separately and seek authorized technical corroboration.
opportunities.query: student identity fraud bots artificial intelligence
opportunities.submission_path: Comparative case study and methods paper

opportunities.title: Fraud prevention and legitimate student access
opportunities.question: Do stronger identity controls reduce fraud while increasing verification delays or false positives for legitimate students?
opportunities.design: Prospective institutional study with authorized aggregate outcomes, an identified comparison period, and separate fraud and access measures. Public reports alone cannot establish causal effects.

opportunities.title: Enrollment incentives and fragmented institutional oversight
opportunities.question: How do funding incentives and divided responsibilities affect the verification of genuine educational participation?
opportunities.design: Structured comparison across United States aid systems, UK university franchising, and Australian vocational providers. Preserve differences in funding and law; do not assume a shared AI mechanism.
opportunities.query: student finance fraud college franchise integrity

opportunities.title: Administrative labels and model learning errors
opportunities.question: Can unresolved application flags become misleading fraud labels that reproduce exclusion when used in machine learning?
opportunities.design: Audit label provenance and compare administrative flags with independently resolved outcomes. The 2021 California memorandum motivates a hypothesis; it does not establish that model contamination occurred.
metrics: precision and recall on independent cases
